diagramDescription: An idea becomes a model. Three branches show how I use it to build an app, modify a game or construct a geometric figure. The signals and checkpoints illustrate the process.
intro: I bring AI into business processes starting from data, develop apps and tools, create video game mods, and pursue independent mathematical research.
aboutStudies: A love of science since childhood, and a stubborn need to understand anything that isn’t clear to me, led me to study physics at university, where my passion for computing grew too: I’ve always found it too fascinating a tool not to explore everything it can do.
aboutWork: From there I took specialist courses in blockchain, data science, machine learning and generative AI, and worked first as a data scientist, then as a data engineer. Today I handle AI and IT across two companies in the same group, working specifically with the R&D team of a chemical company that develops cosmetic formulations and, in parallel, with the parent company’s CFO and CIO on its active investments.
aboutApproach: What I love about my work is that it lets me create value through the way I see things: when I face a problem, I always try to abstract it and reduce it to the most general, deterministic form possible, so the solutions that come out are as simple as they are meaningful. Outside work I do the same, and when something wastes my time I build the tool that fixes it. That’s how I made apps like Social Viewer, which opens social media links directly, without installing each platform’s app or getting pulled into the feed, and the mods I wished existed, which I built and published for anyone looking for them too.
aboutSpare: Through all of this I always find time for my passions and for putting my studies to use, tutoring maths and physics for anyone who needs it and pursuing independent mathematical research, which has led to two papers on arXiv.
philosophy: I want to keep learning, test my ideas and make open-source tools that others can use.

researchPageLead: How small can the circle at the centre of a ring of circles be?
researchReproText: GitHub hosts the code, certificates and independent verifier. Use the Zenodo DOI to cite the archived software release.
geckoPageLead: A Pokédex and an assistant for the Pokémon game you’re playing.
geckoOverviewText: Prof. Gecko combines a searchable Pokémon reference with answers to questions in everyday language. The app is available in Italian and English.
geckoRagText: Before answering, the RAG assistant retrieves documents for the game version and generation you selected.
geckoToolsText: Look up a Pokémon in the Pokédex, explore the Data Hub and compare Pokémon as you put a team together in the Team Builder.
geckoAccessText: Maurizio Falconi (falker47) developed Prof. Gecko. The web app is public and its source code is private.
camaPageLead: A social deduction game for 3–12 people sharing one phone.
camaCardsText: Enter the players’ names and choose which roles to include. Take turns looking at your card in private. Civilians share a word, Moles get a similar one and the Chameleon has to bluff.
camaClueText: Each player says a word or short phrase. Give the other Civilians enough to recognise your clue while keeping the secret word from the Chameleon.
camaVoteText: Compare clues and vote on whom to eliminate. Play continues until the Civilians or the impostors win, then the game awards points.
camaOfflineText: After the first load you can play offline. Install the web app (PWA) on a compatible device or get the Android version from Google Play.
usesPageLead: The equipment I use at home, at my desk and on the road.
usesImageAlt: Illustration of a portable monitor, a router, a charger and a camera with a solar panel.
usesEditorialText: I only add physical products or digital tools where I can provide useful context. When a purchase is involved, prices change, so I do not publish static prices and always point to the source for current terms.
usesDisclosure: As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.
usesRouterText: With good mobile reception indoors, this router turns a data SIM into home Wi-Fi. Compare the data allowance and monthly cost with your fixed-line plan.
usesMonitorText: It fits in my backpack and gives me a second screen when I’m working away from home. On my PC the supplied USB-C cable carries both video and power.
usesChargerText: I charge several devices from one power adapter. GaN packs a lot of power into a small charger, which saves space in my bag.
usesCameraText: I get motion alerts and can speak through the camera from my phone. With enough sunlight I rarely need to recharge it. Alerts and remote control need Wi-Fi.

researchProgramSummary: Ringmin asks how small the central circle can be. The first paper certifies solutions for finite cases. The second describes what happens as the number of circles grows.
researchPaperITitle: Minimum central circles: chain order, seam obstructions, and exact finite certification
researchPaperISummary: The paper reduces circle ordering to a Supnick/anti-Monge traveling salesman problem. Explicit certificates and an independent verifier let readers reproduce the results.
researchPaperIITitle: Minimum central circles: an effective characterization of the global asymptotic constant
researchPaperIISummary: Finite linear programs on balanced words characterize C* with a rigorous error bound that tends to zero. Finding an elementary closed form or an efficient way to evaluate C* remains open.

softwareIntro: I build web and Android apps, tools and games, from the first idea to release. The code of almost every project is on GitHub.
moddingIntro: I make mods for games such as Skyrim and Hogwarts Legacy and translate other authors' mods into Italian. All of them are published on Nexus Mods.
researchIntro: I pursue independent mathematical research on the minimum central circle problem. Every result is checked with reproducible algorithms and certificates and the code is public.
ringminGridLabel: The twelve certified optimal configurations, from n = 3 to n = 14: circles of radius 1 to n arranged around the central circle.
ringminChartLabel: One spoke for each n from 3 to 18, as long as R(n)/n²: the spokes lengthen towards the semicircle of the asymptotic constant C*, as thick as its certified interval. Certified values up to n = 14 are solid, the others dashed.
deckIssuers: Microsoft, IBM, Google, Wharton, UC San Diego and others
deckHintHover: Hover over a certificate or click it to open it.
deckHintTouch: Tap the deck to browse them.
paperITitle: Exact certification of the finite cases
paperIHighlight: Certified global optimum for every n from 3 to 14, with rational bounds less than 10⁻¹¹ apart.
paperILine: Optimal chain order, seam obstructions classified for k = 1, 2, 3, and certificates that do not depend on floating point.
paperIIHighlight: R*(n) = C* n² + o(n²), with C* computable to any precision.
paperIILine: Finite linear programs enclose C* in an arbitrarily narrow interval; the explicit lower bound exceeds 1/8.
lessonsText: My passion for science made me want to teach it too, and since 2023 I’ve been helping middle and high school students in Parma and online. We start wherever you get stuck: I explain every step in full, with digital notes and guided exercises that you keep after the lesson.
lessonsLead: Curious what my students say? These are the sites where I teach.
